identificationModule.briefTitle: Walking and Thinking - Brain Activity During Complex Walking in People With Multiple Sclerosis
identificationModule.officialTitle: Walking and Thinking - Brain Activity During Complex Walking in People With Multiple Sclerosis

descriptionModule.briefSummary:
Every-day life means being part of a complex environment and performing complex tasks that usually involve a combination of motor and cognitive skills. However, the process of aging or the sequelae of neurological diseases such as Multiple Sclerosis (MS) compromises motor-cognitive interaction necessary for an independent lifestyle. While motor-cognitive performance has been identified as an important goal for sustained health across different clinical populations, little is known about underlying brain function leading to these difficulties and how to best target these motor-cognitive difficulties in the context of rehabilitation and exercise interventions.

The challenge of improving treatments of motor-cognitive difficulties (such as dual-tasking and navigation) is daunting, and an important step is arriving at a method that accurately portrays these impairments in an ecological valid state. The investigators aim therefore to explore brain function during complex walking in MS (in comparison with people with Parkinson's disease and healthy controls) by investigating the effects of neurological disease on motor-cognitive performance and its neural correlates during three conditions of complex walking (dual-task walking, navigation and a combination of both) using non-invasive measures of brain activity (functional near infrared spectrometry, fNIRS) and advanced gait analysis in real time in people with MS (in comparison with people with Parkinson's disease and healthy adults).

armGroups.label: Multiple Sclerosis
armGroups.description: People with Multiple Sclerosis, 18 years or older

interventions.name: No intervention
interventions.description:
Assessment of brain activity with fNIRS and behavioural assessments (motor, motor-cognitive and cognitive) during three complex walking conditions.

1. Dual-task walking with the auditory stroop task.
2. Navigational walking - a course consisting of a distribution of 45 and 90 degrees turns to the left and right
3. Navigational and dual-task walking (condition 1 and 2 together)

primaryOutcomes.description: The measurement of changes in concentration of HbO and HHb in the prefrontal cortex will be assessed using a NIRSPORT 2 (NIRx Medizintechnik, Berlin, Germany) device.
primaryOutcomes.timeFrame: During the test session during all three conditions

primaryOutcomes.description: Gait variables such as stride time and/or velocity will be analyzed with the APDM mobility system.
primaryOutcomes.timeFrame: During the test session during all three conditions

primaryOutcomes.description: Cognitive performance of the dual task will be assessed as errors in the response to the Auditory stroop task.
primaryOutcomes.timeFrame: During the test session during complex walking condition 1 and 3

secondaryOutcomes.description: The cognitive test battery comprised the following tests: The Color-Word Interference Test (CWIT), Verbal Fluency, Trail Making Test (TMT) and Ray Auditory Verbal Learning Test (RAVLT) and Symbol Digit Modalities Test (SDMT). Cognitive function will be assessed as a composite measure of these test together.
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: During the test session, takes about 50 minutes

secondaryOutcomes.description: Verbal function, initiation \& task-set switching with the Verbal Fluency test from D-KEFS (Delis-Kaplan Executive Function System).
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: During the test session, takes about 12 minutes

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Cognitive function - Attention and psychomotor processing speed
secondaryOutcomes.description: Attention and psychomotor processing speed will be assessed with the Trail Making Test (TMT) from D-KEFS (Delis-Kaplan Executive Function System).
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: During the test session, takes about 3 minutes

secondaryOutcomes.description: Episodic memory will be assessed with the Ray Auditory Verbal Learning Test (RAVLT).
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: During the test session, takes about 30 minutes

secondaryOutcomes.description: Cognitive processing speed will be assessed with the Symbol Digit Modalities Test (SDMT)
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: During the test session, takes about 3 minutes

secondaryOutcomes.description: Inhibition \& task-set switching with the The Color-Word Interference Test (CWIT) from D-KEFS (Delis-Kaplan Executive Function System).
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: During the test session, takes about 5 minutes

secondaryOutcomes.description: Assessed with the Frändin-Grimby Scale (score 1-6, higher score=better)
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: Will be answered before the test session in the patients home or during the test session
For one week after the test session

secondaryOutcomes.description: Assessed with the Expanded Disability Status Scale (EDSS). Higher scores=worse/more severe disability
Assessed with the Mini-BESTest (Balance Evaluation Systems test), 0-28p.
Assessed with Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS), 0-24 on the depression and anxiety part respectively. Lower score=better
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: Will be answered before the test session in the patients home or during the test session

secondaryOutcomes.description: Self-assessed walking ability with the WALK-12G.
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: Will be answered before the test session in the patients home or at the test session

secondaryOutcomes.description: Cognitive performance of the dual task will be assessed as the reaction time to respond during Auditory stroop
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: During the test session during dual task conditions

secondaryOutcomes.description: WHO Disability Assessment Schedule (WHODAS) version 2.0, 12 self-assessed questions (12 to 60) more points=worse
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: Will be answered before the test session in the patients home or during the test session

secondaryOutcomes.description: Self-assessed impact of fatigue on physical, cognitive, and psychosocial functioning, with the Modified Fatigue Impact Scale (MFIS). 21 items, scored from 0 to 4. Higher scores indicate a larger impact of fatigue.
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: Will be answered before the test session in the patients home or during the test session

secondaryOutcomes.description: Self-assessed physical and psychological impact of MS on health. 29 items, rated from 1 to 5. Higher score indicates perceived worse physical or psychological impacts of MS, respectively, on health.
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: Will be answered before the test session in the patients home or during the test session

eligibilityModule.eligibilityCriteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* 18 years or older
* with an MS diagnosis according to McDonald criteria
* with the ability to walk without a mobility device for ≥5 minutes continuously.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Disease or condition that affects cognition, gait or balance.
* MS relapse or change of disease-modifying treatment within the past eight weeks.
eligibilityModule.studyPopulation: We are studying complex walking in four different populations, people with Multiple Sclerosis, healthy young adults, healthy elderly and elderly with Parkinson's disease. We have during 2022 completed data collection (ClinicalTrials.gov ID: NCT05218213) of healthy young adults, healthy elderly and elderly with Parkinson's disease. Hence, this registration concerns the MS cohort.
